donors.reason: Sulfonamide kinase inhibitor; high anchor similarity 0.8007 supports transfer despite no histone response data.
JNK inhibitor anthrapyrazolone; anchor similarity 0.7151 supports measured donor transfer for histone perturbation.
Amphetamine-like kinase inhibitor; anchor similarity 0.6099 supports inclusion as measured reference donor.
Pyrazole kinase inhibitor; anchor similarity 0.5795 supports transfer for decoder-selected histone feature.
p38 MAPK inhibitor; anchor similarity 0.5416 supports inclusion among top measured donors.

revised_hypotheses: Dactolisib 1 uM 24 h in A375 may yield reproducible histone perturbation >0.5 log2 vs vehicle, especially at H3K9me2K14ac1, H3K56me0, H3K9me1K14ac0, H3K79me1, H3K18ac0K23ac1, and H3K9me3K14ac0.
The fixed decoder may select MCF7 feature BI10043 (H3K27me3K36me0) with sign -1, so donor transfer should prioritize compounds with high A375 anchor similarity.
Retrieved donor pharmacology supports kinase-inhibitor mechanisms but does not provide measured histone response values; donor selection remains similarity-based, not causal.
unresolved: No measured donor histone response values in A375 or MCF7 are supplied, so transfer reproducibility cannot be verified.
Whether dactolisib or selected donors produce >0.5 log2 histone changes versus vehicle remains untested.
The biological link between PI3K/mTOR or donor kinase inhibition and the decoder-selected H3K27me3K36me0 feature is unresolved.
